S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, injury, or emergency-service response to the regulator within 5 calendar days after learning of it, and provide a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. A serious incident involving death, life-threatening injury, or an ongoing hazard must be reported within 24 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and at least every 3 years thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review and a documented corrective-action plan, including retesting and appropriate customer protections.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a means for customers or emergency responders to request shut-off. For units already installed, manufacturers must provide a compatible remote shut-off capability or an equivalent safe retrofit within 6 years after adoption of this standard, where technically feasible; otherwise, they must notify affected customers and regulators and provide a documented risk-mitigation plan.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Regulators may approve an equivalent fire-mitigation design where evidence demonstrates comparable or better safety performance.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If a model’s thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 units of that model installed during a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting data. A recall is mandatory when the regulator determines that a serious risk cannot be adequately controlled through corrective measures, or that required corrective measures have not been completed.

document.section_notes: S1 requires reporting fire, thermal runaway, injury, or emergency response within 5 days (serious within 24h) but excludes minor overheating/smoke. S2 sets a 55°C test and a 5% review threshold with numerical disclosure to customers but no public publication and no automatic sales ban. S3 requires new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit deadline with a feasibility escape; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months with equivalent allowed; S5 has an 8/100k review trigger but recall only on regulator determination, with prompt notices.
